**Pipeline controller notification**
This repo is configured to use the [pipeline controller](https://docs.ci.openshift.org/how-tos/creating-a-pipeline/). Second-stage tests will be triggered either automatically or after lgtm label is added, depending on the repository configuration. The pipeline controller will automatically detect which contexts are required and will utilize `/test` Prow commands to trigger the second stage.

For optional jobs, comment `/test ?` to see a list of all defined jobs. To trigger manually all jobs from second stage use `/pipeline required` command. 

This repository is configured in: LGTM mode

Skipping CI for Draft Pull Request.
If you want CI signal for your change, please convert it to an actual PR.
You can still manually trigger a test run with `/test all`

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8052):

>## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>Pre-installs golangci-lint v2.11.1 and the kube-api-linter Go plugin in the GitHub Actions runner image (`Dockerfile.github-actions-runner`) so they don't need to be rebuilt from source on every lint workflow run.
>
>**Measured impact:** ~49 seconds saved per lint run (37s golangci-lint + 12s kube-api-linter). With ~78 lint runs/week, this eliminates ~3.5-4.5 hours/month of redundant tool compilation.
>
>**How it works:**
>- The Dockerfile now `COPY`s `hack/tools/` and builds both tools during image build, storing them at `/opt/lint-tools/`
>- The lint workflow copies the pre-built binaries to `hack/tools/bin/` and `touch`es them so Make skips the build targets
>- A guard (`if [ -d /opt/lint-tools ]`) ensures graceful fallback to building from source until the new image is deployed
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
>
>Fixes [CNTRLPLANE-3050](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNTRLPLANE-3050)
>
>## Special notes for your reviewer:
>
>- The workflow change is backwards-compatible: if `/opt/lint-tools` doesn't exist (old runner image), lint falls back to building tools from source as before
>- The Makefile rules `$(GOLANGCI_LINT): $(TOOLS_DIR)/go.mod` skip building when the binary exists and is newer than `go.mod` — the `touch` in the workflow ensures this
>- The Go plugin (`.so`) must be built with the same Go version that golangci-lint was built with, which is guaranteed since both are built from the same `hack/tools/go.mod` with the same Go toolchain
>
>## Checklist:
>- [x] Subject and description added to both, commit and PR.
>- [x] Relevant issues have been referenced.
>- [ ] This change includes docs.
>- [ ] This change includes unit tests.
>

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

Builds now produce prebuilt lint artifacts into /opt/lint-tools (Dockerfile), and the GitHub Actions lint workflow conditionally copies those artifacts into hack/tools/bin before running make lint. Several Tekton PipelineRun annotations were updated to add path-based CEL trigger logic and explicit Containerfile path checks. A new CLI tool hack/tools/check-konflux-triggers was added to compute git changed files and evaluate .tekton pull-request CEL expressions locally. A pipeline parameter `hermetic` (default "true") was added and propagated; some PipelineRuns set it to "false".

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Dev as Developer (PR)
  participant GH as GitHub Actions
  participant Docker as Docker build
  participant Repo as Git Repository
  participant LintBin as hack/tools/bin
  participant Make as make lint
  participant CLI as check-konflux-triggers
  participant Git as git
  participant Parser as .tekton YAML reader
  participant CEL as CEL evaluator
  participant Tekton as Tekton Pipelines

  Dev->>Repo: push PR
  GH->>Repo: checkout PR
  GH->>Docker: use image (contains /opt/lint-tools)
  Docker-->>GH: /opt/lint-tools present
  GH->>LintBin: copy golangci-lint & kube-api-linter.so (if present)
  GH->>Make: run make lint
  Dev->>CLI: (optional) run check-konflux-triggers
  CLI->>Git: git diff --name-only base...HEAD
  CLI->>Parser: load .tekton/*pull-request*.yaml
  Parser-->>CLI: return CEL expressions
  CLI->>CEL: compile & evaluate (pathChanged uses changed files)
  CEL-->>CLI: result (YES / no / ERROR)
  CLI-->>Dev: print results (exit non-zero on errors)
  Tekton->>Parser: evaluate CEL for pipeline triggering (includes Containerfile checks)
  Tekton-->>Repo: trigger PipelineRuns (params include hermetic)
```

</details>

<!-- walkthrough_end -->

>Adds a Go tool (`hack/tools/check-konflux-triggers/`) that evaluates Pipelines as Code CEL expressions from `.tekton/*pull-request*` files against the current branch's changed files. Uses the same `gobwas/glob` library as PaC for `pathChanged()` matching and the `google/cel-go` engine for CEL evaluation.
>
>Usage: `go run ./hack/tools/check-konflux-triggers/ [base_ref]`
>
>### 3. Fix Konflux pipeline CEL triggers
>
>The operator-main, release-mce-217, and cli-mce-217 pull-request pipelines were triggering unnecessarily on PRs that only changed files irrelevant to their builds (e.g., GitHub Actions workflows, tooling scripts, other images' Dockerfiles).

>- Added `.github/`, `hack/`, `.claude/`, `Dockerfile.*`, and `Containerfile.*` to the exclusion regex
>- Each pipeline explicitly allows its own Containerfile via a `pathChanged()` clause
>- The cli-mce-217 pipeline previously had **no path filter at all** and triggered on every PR to main
